review_candidates.title: Graduate Trainee, Talent Acquisition Operations & Administration
review_candidates.description: Who We Are AngloGold Ashanti is a global gold mining company with a diverse, high-quality portfolio of operations, projects and exploration activities across 10 countries on four continents. We pursue value-creating opportunities involving other minerals, where we can leverage our existing assets, shareholdings, skills, and experience. At AngloGold Ashanti, we assure you of work that carries significance and creates tangible results. What we do goes beyond mining. We build livelihoods in communities, champion environmental stewardship, and strengthen local and national economies. Our leaders and teams are committed to listening to and supporting each other, valuing differences, and embracing equity. We are convinced that greatness only happens when we prioritize these behaviors and the well-being of every person. Working under the direct guidance of the Talent Acquisition Specialist, the Trainee will provide vital day-to-day administrative and operational support to ensure the smooth execution of the recruitment lifecycle. This immersive program serves as a practical learning platform, enabling a highly organized and analytical graduate to transition from academic theory to corporate execution. By supporting critical Talent Acquisition projects and managing essential onboarding workflows, the Trainee will master enterprise-grade HR technology and develop the foundational capability required for a progressive career in Human Resources. Key Responsibilities Maintain and update recruitment information on the OneHR Recruiting platform, ensuring real-time accuracy of candidate statuses and compliance records. Assist in generating recruitment reports and system data to track key performance metrics (such as Time-to-Fill and source effectiveness) across our operating sites. Support recruiters in building structured talent pools within SuccessFactors for future hiring needs. Conduct initial resume screenings to identify qualified applicants for further review. Assist recruiters in performing initial phone screenings or basic evaluation calls for entry-level and high-volume roles. Help organize and set up digital assessment centers or group interviews as required. Schedule interviews (virtual via MS Teams and face-to-face) across multiple regional sites and time zones. Manage calendar invites for candidates and busy hiring panels, ensuring all necessary links, interview guides, and resumes are available. Provide proactive support on key Talent Acquisition projects (such as employer branding initiatives, system optimization trials, or regional recruitment campaigns). Assist in preparing pre-employment paperwork, coordinating background checks, and tracking onboarding readiness. review_candidates.title: Finance Manager
review_candidates.description: Who We Are Nee Tahi Buhn First Nation is located on the south shore of Francois Lake in beautiful British Columbia. With deep roots in our land, language, and traditions, we are proud to be a vibrant and resilient community. Our Nation is home to approximately 140 members, and we are committed to preserving our rich heritage while building a strong future for the next generations. At Nee Tahi Buhn, we believe in creating a positive, respectful, and supportive environment where both community and team members can thrive. We honour our past and work toward a bright future built on cultural strength and community well-being. Overview Of The Role The Finance Manager provides hands-on and strategic financial leadership for Nee Tahi Buhn Indian Band. This role is responsible for strengthening financial planning, budgeting, reporting, audit readiness, internal controls and financial administration practices across the organization. Working closely with the General Manager, Chief and Council, managers, employees, funders, auditors and external advisors, the Finance Manager will help establish clear financial processes, support responsible decision-making, and build financial capacity throughout the organization. This is a foundational leadership role for the Band. The successful candidate will bring strong technical finance skills, a practical and organized approach, and the ability to explain financial information clearly to people with varying levels of financial knowledge. The role requires someone who can respectfully support managers and leadership to understand budgets, monitor variances, strengthen accountability and make informed decisions that protect the Nation’s resources and support long-term sustainability. Location: Band office and community, Burns Lake, BC Employment Status: Full-time, permanent Reports to: General Manager, with advisory and reporting relationship to Chief and Council Compensation: $80k-90k/year Key Responsibilities Lead annual and long-term budgeting, financial planning, forecasting and cash flow management. Prepare clear and timely financial reports, variance analysis, dashboards and briefing materials for leadership, funders, Chief and Council. Provide practical financial advice to support responsible decision-making, accountability and the sustainable use of resources across the organization. Oversee day-to-day finance operations, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, reconciliations, general ledger, purchasing, cash management and financial records. Strengthen internal controls, approval processes, documentation, financial policies and procedures. Monitor funding agreements, reporting deadlines, eligible expenditures and compliance requirements. Support funding applications, budgets, claims, reports and related financial documentation. Lead audit preparation, year-end close, working papers, and responses to auditor requests. Identify financial risks, reporting gaps, audit findings and control issues, and recommending practical solutions. Supervise, coach and support finance staff, including work planning, training, and performance management. Build financial understanding across the organization by supporting managers and employees to understand budgets, reports, coding and funding restrictions. Model confidentiality, professionalism, accountability, patience and service-oriented leadership. What You Bring Skills & Qualifications Post-secondary education in accounting, finance, business administration or a related field; an equivalent combination of education, training and progressive experience may be considered. Minimum of five years of progressive finance and accounting experience. Minimum of two years of leadership or supervisory experience. Experience with budgeting, cash flow forecasting, asset management, audit preparation, funding agreements, payroll, financial policies, and internal controls. Strong knowledge of financial reporting, variance analysis, reconciliations, and financial administration practices. Proficiency in MS Excel, data analysis and systems. Ability to build effective working relationships with various stakeholders. Professionalism and ability to communicate complex financial information to diverse audiences. Ability to maintain strict confidentiality. Preferred CPA designation. Experience working with a First Nation government, Indigenous organization or community-based organization. Experience with Adagio and PayDirt software. What We Offer Extended health and dental benefits after 90 days of employment. Three weeks of vacation to start. Two weeks paid time off over the Christmas holidays. Every second Friday is a half day, with a paid half day off. 12 paid sick days per year. 5 unpaid cultural days per year. Opportunities for professional development. A supportive and community-focused work environment. To Apply Interested candidates are invited to submit a resume and cover letter outlining how their experience and qualifications align with this opportunity. The successful candidate will be required to provide references, proof of qualifications, and a satisfactory criminal record check. We encourage applicants to apply as soon as possible, as applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis. Persons of Indigenous ancestry will be given preference pursuant to Section 16(1) of the Canadian Human Rights Act.

review_candidates.title: Engineering Graduate, Bridges (Hiring Day Event ON)
review_candidates.description: Job Description Are you graduating in Spring 2027 and ready to take the first step in your professional journey? Join us for our in-person Hiring Day event at our Toronto office ( October 27th ) or Waterloo office ( October 29th ). This is a unique opportunity to connect with GHD professionals, learn more about our work and culture, and explore exciting career opportunities. If you're interested in participating in our Hiring Day and being considered for an Engineering Graduate, Bridges role, we encourage you to review the job description below and apply if it aligns with your career goals. As part of the selection process, you'll be invited to complete a HireVue video interview and answer a few pre-screening questions. Candidates who successfully progress through the initial screening stage will be contacted by our recruitment team and invited to move forward in the Hiring Day process. Help us shape a more sustainable, resilient, and connected future. At GHD, our Design & Delivery Organisation (DDO) teams work across a diverse range of projects that support the delivery of essential infrastructure, buildings, transportation networks, environmental solutions, water systems, and energy assets. By combining technical expertise, innovation, and collaboration, we help our clients solve complex challenges and deliver lasting value to the communities they serve. Join our global network of professionals and be part of a team that is committed to making a positive impact while providing opportunities for professional growth and career development. What we´re looking for: We're seeking graduates who are eager to learn, passionate about making a positive impact, and excited to contribute to meaningful projects that shape the future of our communities. As an Engineering Graduate, you will work alongside experienced professionals to support the planning, design, and delivery of a wide range of engineering projects. Applying the knowledge gained through your studies, you will assist in solving engineering challenges while contributing to high-quality outcomes for our clients and the communities they serve. This role will work on the design and construction of bridges, culverts, retaining walls and other transportation-related structures specifically on projects in partnership with MTO (Ministry of Transportation) and municipalities. They will also undertake bridge inspections, investigations and assessment report preparation. Moreover, you will be someone who flourishes in a fast-paced and challenging environment with an equally supportive team striving together towards project excellence . Through mentorship, collaboration, and hands-on experience, you will build technical capability, strengthen your problem-solving skills, and develop an understanding of industry’s best practices. We're looking for graduates who demonstrate curiosity, initiative, and a collaborative mindset, with strong communication skills and a commitment to continuous learning. The successful candidate will be motivated to grow professionally, contribute to team success, and help deliver innovative and sustainable solutions that create lasting value for our clients and communities. This position can be based in St Catharines, Whitby, Markham, Toronto or Mississauga. Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in office, three days a week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment. Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in: Management (External): Help senior colleagues manage client and customer relationships by using relevant sales or client systems. Community of Practice Management: Participate in a community of practice in a defined area of expertise or consulting to begin to build own expertise. Contract document preparation for a variety of transportation-related projects involving transportation structures; Cost estimating including life cycle cost analysis and construction cost estimates Data Collection and Analysis: Produce accurate reports for others by collecting data from a variety of standard sources and inputting it into standard formats. Execute design calculations for structural designs and evaluations. Engineering Drawings: Create engineering drawings to support the communication, evaluation, and implementation of engineering solutions. Preparation of preliminary and detailed designs of bridges, culverts and other transportation-related structures; Engineering Solutions Design: Contribute to the development of , and implement feasibility testing of , proposed engineering solutions to provide feedback and data to validate the design. Health, Safety, and Environment: Follow the organization's health, safety, and environment (HSE) policies, procedures, and mandatory instructions to identify and mitigate environmental risks and risks to the well-being of self and others in the workplace; instruct the team in safe working methods; identify instances of risky behaviors within the team and take appropriate action, escalating serious issues as appropriate. Inspection of existing bridges, culverts and retaining walls to confirm existing conditions, preparing reports, and organizing large quantities of inspection data. Liaise with contractors and owners during design and construction; Personal Capability Building: Develop own capabilities by participating in assessment and development planning activities as well as formal and informal training and coaching. Develop and maintain an understanding of relevant technology, external regulation, and industry best practices through ongoing education, attending conferences, and reading specialist media. Project Management: Support others by carrying out a range of project management activities. Request for Bid Solicitation/Proposal/Tender Response: Gather information and resources to assist in the drafting of standardized tenders/proposals in response to bid solicitations, request for proposal, and request for tender. What You Will Bring To The Team A recent or upcoming University degree in civil / structural engineering 0-2 years of experience related to the role Strong problem-solving and analytical skills with the ability to think critically and approach challenges with curiosity.
